title: Cross-implementation: each endpoint parses the other's envelopes; identical inputs give identical bytes
summary: Offline, both endpoints build every vector of docs/test-vectors.json that has inputs and run every receiver case; the bytes and the dispositions are compared with each other and with the vector file. Live, both endpoints exchange envelopes of all five priorities, header-only envelopes, envelopes with ACK_REQ, envelopes of 30000 and 65536 bytes (Endpoint A) and 65000 bytes (Endpoint B), an unprotected envelope with an unknown frame type (Endpoint A), and signed envelopes with an unknown frame type, one of them a command (Endpoint B; Earth-MCC signs every envelope that has a payload, SPEC-DIGEST A38). Both endpoints log the bytes of every envelope (--log-hex-max 65580), and each endpoint's offline tool decodes every envelope the other logged as sent and compares every header field, the length and the SHA-256 with the sender's own record.

criteria.text: For every vector with inputs, Endpoint A and Endpoint B build the same bytes, equal to the vector file; for every receiver and SEC-B case both give the expected result and reason

criteria.name: a-vectors
criteria.text: Endpoint A's vector run passes every check

criteria.name: vector-comparison

criteria.name: a-crosscheck
criteria.text: Endpoint A decodes every envelope Endpoint B logged as sent (all have envelope_hex) with the same field values, and Endpoint B received every envelope A sent, byte-identical (the tool fails otherwise)

criteria.name: b-crosscheck
criteria.text: Endpoint B decodes every envelope Endpoint A logged as sent (all have envelope_hex) with the same field values, and Endpoint A received every envelope B sent, byte-identical (the tool fails otherwise)
Every envelope handed to ION is received by the other endpoint
Every received envelope is byte-identical to the envelope handed to ION
Each endpoint accepts every envelope of the other implementation
The protected command with an unknown frame type is executed
